title: 223. no one tells you this career advice (how to *actually* get ahead at work) feat. dr. rosalind chow
description_html:
today’s guest is dr. rosalind chow— an associate professor of organizational behavior and theory at carnegie mellon university who studies the power of social hierarchy and its impact on diversity and inclusion efforts within organizations. her recently published book, the doors you can open, revolutionizes the way we network in the workplace.

in this episode, we break down what work mentors & sponsors look like (and how you can land one yourself!) and how inequality affects the workplace.

the challenges in trying to change workplace inequalities

summary: sadie sits down with dr. rosalind chow, an organizational behavior professor at carnegie mellon, to talk about mentorship, sponsorship, and navigating workplace inequality. they break down the difference between mentors (who help you grow) and sponsors (who advocate for you to others), why sponsorship matters for women and people of color, and how to build these relationships without feeling like you have nothing to offer. dr. chow also explains why structural change is so hard, how to talk about inequality without triggering defensiveness, and why celebrating others' strengths—instead of comparing yourself—is the real skill that sets you up for long-term success.
quote: there's value in the problems that you can help other people solve, and value in having problems that other people can help you solve too.
